responseText:
Short answer: archiving keeps the messages but removes them from your Inbox; deleting a label removes that label from the messages but does not delete the messages themselves. (If by “deleting it” you actually mean deleting the messages, that is different — see below.)

Details and consequences
- Archive (select messages with the label and click Archive): removes the Inbox label from those messages. Messages remain in All Mail and keep any other labels (including "contracts 2019" if you archive from Inbox but don’t remove that label). They’re still searchable and reachable by label or search. Easily undone by selecting messages and choosing “Move to Inbox.”
- Delete the label (Settings → Labels → Remove label): the label name is removed from your account and from every message that had it. The messages themselves remain in All Mail (and with any other labels they had) and are still searchable, but you lose that label-based organization. Recreating the label does not automatically reassign it to the old messages.
- Delete the messages (Move to Trash / Delete): moves messages to Trash; they’re recoverable for up to ~30 days, then permanently deleted. This is the destructive option.

What could go wrong
- If you delete the label, you lose the organizational tag and will have to relabel messages manually or via a script; there’s no built-in “undo label removal” that restores the label to the same set automatically.
- If you archive, messages may be less visible in your Inbox and you might miss time-sensitive items.
- If you delete messages, you risk permanent loss after the Trash retention period.

Who will see the result
- Changes affect your account and anyone who has access/delegation to it. They are not visible to other unrelated accounts.

Can it be undone
- Archive: easily undone.
- Remove label: not automatically undone; you can recreate the label but must reapply it manually or with a script/filter.
- Delete messages: reversible from Trash for a limited time (~30 days); permanent afterward.

Quick check before you act
Which exactly do you mean by “delete it”: remove the label from messages, or delete the messages themselves? If you want me to perform a destructive action later, tell me the exact target (label name or number of messages), the exact action, and explicitly confirm — I won’t run anything until you confirm.
